A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Visual Generation Without Guidance and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4, Tables 2–4, and Appendix C report original GFT fine-tuning, training-from-scratch, efficiency, and image-generation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original GFT experiments and reports additional SD1.5 guidance-distillation comparisons and precision–recall results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same interpolation, stop-gradient operation, temperature conditioning, and guidance-free inference. Corrections to conditional versus sampling symbols in Section 3.3 repair the mathematical description without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-256 for class-conditional generation, LAION-Aesthetic 5+ for text-to-image training, and COCO 2014 for evaluation. The larger reported LAION subset changes sample count, not demonstrated task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Figure 8 add guidance distillation by Meng et al. (2023) to the SD1.5 comparison. V1 already evaluated this method with DiT, but not in the corresponding SD1.5 experiment. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 revises the LAION subset from 12.8 million to 18 million pairs. Appendix D changes SD1.5 fine-tuning from 50,000 to 70,000 updates and EMA decay from 0.999 to 0.9999. V2 also adds precision–recall evaluation and an SD1.5 distillation experiment with guidance scales 1–14; the broader evaluation framework remains intact.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds precision–recall trade-off analyses for fine-tuned DiT-XL/2 and LlamaGen-3B, and from-scratch DiT-B/2 and LlamaGen-L, in Figures 11–12. These supplement the existing diversity–fidelity analyses. Figure 8 also extends the SD1.5 trade-off comparison to distillation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports explicit repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark scores. The added trade-off curves do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes SD1.5 CFG/GFT FIDs from 8.30/8.32 to 7.87/8.10 and adds distillation at 8.16. Figure 8 and Section 5.4 add the reported CLIP-score advantage over distillation; Figure 9 revises VAR-d30 GFT trade-off points; Figures 11–12 add precision–recall results. SD1.5 training conditions differ between versions, so its lower FIDs are not same-setting gains. Tables 2 and 4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 10–12 correct sampling-model symbols to conditional-model symbols, removing the self-referential logit definition in v1. Appendix B explicitly qualifies the stop-gradient argument with beta in (0, 1]. The main theorem and proof strategy remain otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: GFT supports fine-tuning and training from scratch, matches CFG quality while halving sampling computation, and provides adjustable diversity–fidelity trade-offs across diffusion, autoregressive, and masked models.

C2.justification: The explanations based on end-to-end training, maximum-likelihood convergence, and matching CFG’s sampling distribution remain unchanged. The computational restriction to smaller from-scratch models and the MAR temperature-schedule qualification are retained. New comparative findings do not add substantive mechanism explanations or limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds SD1.5 distillation settings, including guidance scales 1–14 and alignment of other hyperparameters with GFT, and revises the documented update count and EMA decay. The abstract replaces the future code-release promise with a direct code listing; actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands discussion of guidance-free alternatives to perceptual losses, score-based distillation, and consistency models, with additional foundational diffusion and guidance citations. The citation to Improved Distribution Matching Distillation is removed. The principal positioning against guidance distillation and CCA remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is revised, and the discrete CFG explanation moves from Section 3.3 to Section 2.2 under separate continuous/discrete headings. Publication, correspondence, and acknowledgement text is updated. The overall section structure and most substantive prose are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds two precision–recall figures and a distillation row/curve, moves the CFG/GFT schematic to page 1, reorders Figure 4 panels, relocates Figure 6, and adds equation references to Table 1. Existing qualitative appendix figures are retained and renumbered, with smaller axis, legend, and layout adjustments elsewhere.

improvement.justification: The added SD1.5 distillation comparison and appendix precision–recall analyses modestly strengthen evidence for the existing claims. Corrected conditional-logit definitions and broader related-work coverage improve clarity and completeness. These are limited gains around an unchanged contribution; the revised SD1.5 training conditions prevent treating its lower FID as evidence of methodological improvement.
